chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah, from some of his companions, from Abi Basir, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'A woman comes performing Tamattu' Hajj, then she becomes menstruating before she performs Tawaf al-Ifadah (the circumambulation for release) with the Kaaba, so her purity falls on the night of Arafat.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'If she knows that she will become pure, perform Tawaf with the House, and be released from her Ihram, and join the people, then let her do so.'

key_terms.مُتَمِّعَةً: Performing Tamattu' Hajj (combining Umrah and Hajj)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a menstruating woman performing Tamattu' Hajj who becomes pure on the night of Arafat?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Istibsar clarifies the ruling for a woman in Tamattu' Hajj whose menstruation ends on the night of Arafat, just before the critical Tawaf al-Ifadah. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) emphasizes the condition of certainty ('if she knows') regarding her purity and ability to complete the rites, highlighting the Shia juristic focus on practical feasibility and avoiding the loss of Hajj validity. This ruling underscores the importance of timing in the completion of Hajj pillars, distinguishing between mere possibility and assured capability.
